<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

Rust only. Tap ownership: crates/tmux/src/lib.rs (~L835-900, `pane_pipe`/@pij-tap-sink marker logic; TAP_SINK_OPTION L42). Observer loop: crates/daemon/src/pane_observer.rs (where the refusal is logged per tick). Gate: crates/harnesses/src/interaction.rs refresh_live_tap/fresh_injection_verdict/submit_with_owned_input (L283-378) — add a verdict reason enum (TapUnowned | ComposerBusy | HumanTyping | Unrecognized) instead of a bare bool pair. Delivery: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs ~L231-330 (TypedBody rung → Deferred → enqueue) — carry the reason into the queued receipt (additive `reason` field in DeliveryOutcome::Queued, types.rs) and make the drain re-attempt after tap claim. Legacy tap signature: pane_pipe=1 AND marker empty AND ~/.pij/pane-signals/_<N>.raw exists (legacy sets no marker; it uses `pipe-pane -O -o` so it will NOT clobber a pipe rs owns — verify and cite). Supersede = close pipe (`tmux pipe-pane -t %N`), then claim as today. Do not touch .pi/extensions.

## Isolation

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| mode | solo-pm in the plan worktree |
| note | Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence. |
